- On `IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, `data/fa-tokens.json` on `factory-data` reached **96,174 bytes** (525 legs across 197 keys) at commit `21a0fb08f7da33cc5de24f796da306d551e3418c` (`leg tokens — pr-1665 rework [skip ci]`, `2026-10-19T14:22:28Z`).
- `contentsPutCommand` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` (and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) constructed:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/contents/<dataPath> -f branch=... -f message=... -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
- At 96,174 bytes of raw JSON, base64 encoding (`4/3` + line wraps) produced **129,927 bytes** for the single CLI argument `content=<base64>`. The very next leg pushed `content=<base64>` past the Linux kernel `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit (**131,072 bytes / 128 KiB** per single argument in `execve`), causing `/bin/sh` / `gh` to fail with `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long`) on all 3 retries and silently give up (`::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts`).
- Because `data/fa-tokens.json` froze at `pr-1665`, `fetchTokensFromBranch` had no entries for `pr-1715+`, so `tmap['pr-' + pr.number]` missed on 100% of active cards in `data/fa-state.json`.

## Changes
1. **`js/factory/token_usage.js`**:
   - Added runtime-agnostic `base64EncodeUtf8(str)` and `buildContentsPutBody(o)` (`{ branch, message, content, sha? }`).
   - Added `--input <tempPath>` transport (`tempPutBodyPath`, `contentsPutInputCommand`, `tryPutViaInputFile`, `putTokenContents`) following the `checkRunStamp.js` pattern (`file_write` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input <tempFile>` + `file_delete` in `finally`), keeping the shell command string under 200 bytes regardless of payload size while preserving legacy `contentsPutCommand` fallback when `io.write` is not injected.
2. **`js/factory/token_usage_publish.js`**:
   - Wired `file_write` and `file_delete` into the `publishTokenUsage` IO adapter alongside `cli_execute_command` and `file_read`.
3. **`scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`**:
   - Replaced `-f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)"` with temp files (`jq -n --rawfile next ... '{branch, message, content: ($next | @base64)}'` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input "${BODY_FILE}"`).
4. **`js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js`**:
   - Added unit tests for `base64EncodeUtf8` (ASCII, padding, multi-byte UTF-8), `buildContentsPutBody`, `--input` temp-file lifecycle, and a >100 KB raw JSON (>131,072 bytes base64) regression test verifying the shell command stays <200 bytes.

Closes #1152

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# (step: Publish leg token usage (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)) — stage-1 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block + always() stay on the workflow step.
set -eu
if [ ! -s "${RUN_OUTPUT}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no run output captured — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT SUM_CR MODEL < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = cr = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # fa-tokens carries cacheRead per segment (gh-1241); the
        # board prices it (model-pricing cacheRead rates) and
        # renders an `input cached` column — sum it like in/out.
        cr += int(rec.get("cacheRead") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, cr, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
SUM_CR="${SUM_CR:-0}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-}"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"cacheRead":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${SUM_CR}" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} cached=${SUM_CR} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))' > "${NEXT_FILE}"
  jq -n \
    --rawfile next "${NEXT_FILE}" \
    --arg branch "${DATA_BRANCH}" \
    --arg message "leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]" \
    --arg sha "${SHA}" \
    '{branch: $branch, message: $message, content: ($next | @base64)} + (if $sha != "" then {sha: $sha} else {} end)' > "${BODY_FILE}"
  if gh api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}" --input "${BODY_FILE}"; then ok=1; break; fi
  echo "token publish attempt ${attempt} conflicted — refetching"
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done
if [ "${ok}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts (concurrent writes) — rows are decorative, next legs retry"
fi

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1154
- **Title**: fix(token_usage): use --input temp file for Contents API PUT to avoid E2BIG (#1152)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/gh-1152-tokens-put-e2big` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +301
- **Deletions**: -36
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:26:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T21:54:25Z

## PR Description

## Summary
Fixes the `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long` at Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 131,072 bytes) failure when publishing `data/fa-tokens.json` to `factory-data`.

## Root Cause
- On `IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, `data/fa-tokens.json` on `factory-data` reached **96,174 bytes** (525 legs across 197 keys) at commit `21a0fb08f7da33cc5de24f796da306d551e3418c` (`leg tokens — pr-1665 rework [skip ci]`, `2026-10-19T14:22:28Z`).
- `contentsPutCommand` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` (and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) constructed:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/contents/<dataPath> -f branch=... -f message=... -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
- At 96,174 bytes of raw JSON, base64 encoding (`4/3` + line wraps) produced **129,927 bytes** for the single CLI argument `content=<base64>`. The very next leg pushed `content=<base64>` past the Linux kernel `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit (**131,072 bytes / 128 KiB** per single argument in `execve`), causing `/bin/sh` / `gh` to fail with `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long`) on all 3 retries and silently give up (`::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts`).
- Because `data/fa-tokens.json` froze at `pr-1665`, `fetchTokensFromBranch` had no entries for `pr-1715+`, so `tmap['pr-' + pr.number]` missed on 100% of active cards in `data/fa-state.json`.

## Changes
1. **`js/factory/token_usage.js`**:
   - Added runtime-agnostic `base64EncodeUtf8(str)` and `buildContentsPutBody(o)` (`{ branch, message, content, sha? }`).
   - Added `--input <tempPath>` transport (`tempPutBodyPath`, `contentsPutInputCommand`, `tryPutViaInputFile`, `putTokenContents`) following the `checkRunStamp.js` pattern (`file_write` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input <tempFile>` + `file_delete` in `finally`), keeping the shell command string under 200 bytes regardless of payload size while preserving legacy `contentsPutCommand` fallback when `io.write` is not injected.
2. **`js/factory/token_usage_publish.js`**:
   - Wired `file_write` and `file_delete` into the `publishTokenUsage` IO adapter alongside `cli_execute_command` and `file_read`.
3. **`scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`**:
   - Replaced `-f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)"` with temp files (`jq -n --rawfile next ... '{branch, message, content: ($next | @base64)}'` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input "${BODY_FILE}"`).
4. **`js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js`**:
   - Added unit tests for `base64EncodeUtf8` (ASCII, padding, multi-byte UTF-8), `buildContentsPutBody`, `--input` temp-file lifecycle, and a >100 KB raw JSON (>131,072 bytes base64) regression test verifying the shell command stays <200 bytes.

Closes #1152

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# (step: Publish leg token usage (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)) — stage-1 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block + always() stay on the workflow step.
set -eu
if [ ! -s "${RUN_OUTPUT}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no run output captured — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT SUM_CR MODEL < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = cr = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # fa-tokens carries cacheRead per segment (gh-1241); the
        # board prices it (model-pricing cacheRead rates) and
        # renders an `input cached` column — sum it like in/out.
        cr += int(rec.get("cacheRead") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, cr, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
SUM_CR="${SUM_CR:-0}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-}"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"cacheRead":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${SUM_CR}" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} cached=${SUM_CR} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))' > "${NEXT_FILE}"
  jq -n \
    --rawfile next "${NEXT_FILE}" \
    --arg branch "${DATA_BRANCH}" \
    --arg message "leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]" \
    --arg sha "${SHA}" \
    '{branch: $branch, message: $message, content: ($next | @base64)} + (if $sha != "" then {sha: $sha} else {} end)' > "${BODY_FILE}"
  if gh api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}" --input "${BODY_FILE}"; then ok=1; break; fi
  echo "token publish attempt ${attempt} conflicted — refetching"
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done
if [ "${ok}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts (concurrent writes) — rows are decorative, next legs retry"
fi

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

and gave-up are statuses, not errors (the workflow step runs under
`always()`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1154
- **Title**: fix(token_usage): use --input temp file for Contents API PUT to avoid E2BIG (#1152)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/gh-1152-tokens-put-e2big` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +301
- **Deletions**: -36
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:26:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T21:54:25Z

## PR Description

## Summary
Fixes the `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long` at Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 131,072 bytes) failure when publishing `data/fa-tokens.json` to `factory-data`.

## Root Cause
- On `IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, `data/fa-tokens.json` on `factory-data` reached **96,174 bytes** (525 legs across 197 keys) at commit `21a0fb08f7da33cc5de24f796da306d551e3418c` (`leg tokens — pr-1665 rework [skip ci]`, `2026-10-19T14:22:28Z`).
- `contentsPutCommand` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` (and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) constructed:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/contents/<dataPath> -f branch=... -f message=... -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
- At 96,174 bytes of raw JSON, base64 encoding (`4/3` + line wraps) produced **129,927 bytes** for the single CLI argument `content=<base64>`. The very next leg pushed `content=<base64>` past the Linux kernel `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit (**131,072 bytes / 128 KiB** per single argument in `execve`), causing `/bin/sh` / `gh` to fail with `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long`) on all 3 retries and silently give up (`::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts`).
- Because `data/fa-tokens.json` froze at `pr-1665`, `fetchTokensFromBranch` had no entries for `pr-1715+`, so `tmap['pr-' + pr.number]` missed on 100% of active cards in `data/fa-state.json`.

## Changes
1. **`js/factory/token_usage.js`**:
   - Added runtime-agnostic `base64EncodeUtf8(str)` and `buildContentsPutBody(o)` (`{ branch, message, content, sha? }`).
   - Added `--input <tempPath>` transport (`tempPutBodyPath`, `contentsPutInputCommand`, `tryPutViaInputFile`, `putTokenContents`) following the `checkRunStamp.js` pattern (`file_write` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input <tempFile>` + `file_delete` in `finally`), keeping the shell command string under 200 bytes regardless of payload size while preserving legacy `contentsPutCommand` fallback when `io.write` is not injected.
2. **`js/factory/token_usage_publish.js`**:
   - Wired `file_write` and `file_delete` into the `publishTokenUsage` IO adapter alongside `cli_execute_command` and `file_read`.
3. **`scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`**:
   - Replaced `-f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)"` with temp files (`jq -n --rawfile next ... '{branch, message, content: ($next | @base64)}'` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input "${BODY_FILE}"`).
4. **`js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js`**:
   - Added unit tests for `base64EncodeUtf8` (ASCII, padding, multi-byte UTF-8), `buildContentsPutBody`, `--input` temp-file lifecycle, and a >100 KB raw JSON (>131,072 bytes base64) regression test verifying the shell command stays <200 bytes.

Closes #1152

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# (step: Publish leg token usage (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)) — stage-1 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block + always() stay on the workflow step.
set -eu
if [ ! -s "${RUN_OUTPUT}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no run output captured — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT SUM_CR MODEL < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = cr = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # fa-tokens carries cacheRead per segment (gh-1241); the
        # board prices it (model-pricing cacheRead rates) and
        # renders an `input cached` column — sum it like in/out.
        cr += int(rec.get("cacheRead") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, cr, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
SUM_CR="${SUM_CR:-0}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-}"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"cacheRead":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${SUM_CR}" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} cached=${SUM_CR} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))' > "${NEXT_FILE}"
  jq -n \
    --rawfile next "${NEXT_FILE}" \
    --arg branch "${DATA_BRANCH}" \
    --arg message "leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]" \
    --arg sha "${SHA}" \
    '{branch: $branch, message: $message, content: ($next | @base64)} + (if $sha != "" then {sha: $sha} else {} end)' > "${BODY_FILE}"
  if gh api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}" --input "${BODY_FILE}"; then ok=1; break; fi
  echo "token publish attempt ${attempt} conflicted — refetching"
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done
if [ "${ok}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts (concurrent writes) — rows are decorative, next legs retry"
fi

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1154
- **Title**: fix(token_usage): use --input temp file for Contents API PUT to avoid E2BIG (#1152)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/gh-1152-tokens-put-e2big` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +301
- **Deletions**: -36
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:26:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T21:54:25Z

## PR Description

## Summary
Fixes the `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long` at Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 131,072 bytes) failure when publishing `data/fa-tokens.json` to `factory-data`.

## Root Cause
- On `IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, `data/fa-tokens.json` on `factory-data` reached **96,174 bytes** (525 legs across 197 keys) at commit `21a0fb08f7da33cc5de24f796da306d551e3418c` (`leg tokens — pr-1665 rework [skip ci]`, `2026-10-19T14:22:28Z`).
- `contentsPutCommand` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` (and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) constructed:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/contents/<dataPath> -f branch=... -f message=... -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
- At 96,174 bytes of raw JSON, base64 encoding (`4/3` + line wraps) produced **129,927 bytes** for the single CLI argument `content=<base64>`. The very next leg pushed `content=<base64>` past the Linux kernel `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit (**131,072 bytes / 128 KiB** per single argument in `execve`), causing `/bin/sh` / `gh` to fail with `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long`) on all 3 retries and silently give up (`::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts`).
- Because `data/fa-tokens.json` froze at `pr-1665`, `fetchTokensFromBranch` had no entries for `pr-1715+`, so `tmap['pr-' + pr.number]` missed on 100% of active cards in `data/fa-state.json`.

## Changes
1. **`js/factory/token_usage.js`**:
   - Added runtime-agnostic `base64EncodeUtf8(str)` and `buildContentsPutBody(o)` (`{ branch, message, content, sha? }`).
   - Added `--input <tempPath>` transport (`tempPutBodyPath`, `contentsPutInputCommand`, `tryPutViaInputFile`, `putTokenContents`) following the `checkRunStamp.js` pattern (`file_write` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input <tempFile>` + `file_delete` in `finally`), keeping the shell command string under 200 bytes regardless of payload size while preserving legacy `contentsPutCommand` fallback when `io.write` is not injected.
2. **`js/factory/token_usage_publish.js`**:
   - Wired `file_write` and `file_delete` into the `publishTokenUsage` IO adapter alongside `cli_execute_command` and `file_read`.
3. **`scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`**:
   - Replaced `-f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)"` with temp files (`jq -n --rawfile next ... '{branch, message, content: ($next | @base64)}'` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input "${BODY_FILE}"`).
4. **`js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js`**:
   - Added unit tests for `base64EncodeUtf8` (ASCII, padding, multi-byte UTF-8), `buildContentsPutBody`, `--input` temp-file lifecycle, and a >100 KB raw JSON (>131,072 bytes base64) regression test verifying the shell command stays <200 bytes.

Closes #1152

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# (step: Publish leg token usage (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)) — stage-1 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block + always() stay on the workflow step.
set -eu
if [ ! -s "${RUN_OUTPUT}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no run output captured — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT SUM_CR MODEL < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = cr = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # fa-tokens carries cacheRead per segment (gh-1241); the
        # board prices it (model-pricing cacheRead rates) and
        # renders an `input cached` column — sum it like in/out.
        cr += int(rec.get("cacheRead") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, cr, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
SUM_CR="${SUM_CR:-0}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-}"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"cacheRead":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${SUM_CR}" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} cached=${SUM_CR} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
NEXT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-next.XXXXXX")"
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fa-tokens-body.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "${NEXT_FILE}" "${BODY_FILE}"' EXIT
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))' > "${NEXT_FILE}"
  jq -n \
    --rawfile next "${NEXT_FILE}" \
    --arg branch "${DATA_BRANCH}" \
    --arg message "leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]" \
    --arg sha "${SHA}" \
    '{branch: $branch, message: $message, content: ($next | @base64)} + (if $sha != "" then {sha: $sha} else {} end)' > "${BODY_FILE}"
  if gh api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}" --input "${BODY_FILE}"; then ok=1; break; fi
  echo "token publish attempt ${attempt} conflicted — refetching"
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done
if [ "${ok}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts (concurrent writes) — rows are decorative, next legs retry"
fi

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

    "summary": "fix(token_usage): use --input temp file for Contents API PUT to avoid E2BIG (#1152)",
    "description": "## Summary
Fixes the `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long` at Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 131,072 bytes) failure when publishing `data/fa-tokens.json` to `factory-data`.

## Root Cause
- On `IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, `data/fa-tokens.json` on `factory-data` reached **96,174 bytes** (525 legs across 197 keys) at commit `21a0fb08f7da33cc5de24f796da306d551e3418c` (`leg tokens — pr-1665 rework [skip ci]`, `2026-10-19T14:22:28Z`).
- `contentsPutCommand` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` (and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) constructed:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/contents/<dataPath> -f branch=... -f message=... -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
- At 96,174 bytes of raw JSON, base64 encoding (`4/3` + line wraps) produced **129,927 bytes** for the single CLI argument `content=<base64>`. The very next leg pushed `content=<base64>` past the Linux kernel `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit (**131,072 bytes / 128 KiB** per single argument in `execve`), causing `/bin/sh` / `gh` to fail with `E2BIG` (`Argument list too long`) on all 3 retries and silently give up (`::warning::token publish gave up after 3 attempts`).
- Because `data/fa-tokens.json` froze at `pr-1665`, `fetchTokensFromBranch` had no entries for `pr-1715+`, so `tmap['pr-' + pr.number]` missed on 100% of active cards in `data/fa-state.json`.

## Changes
1. **`js/factory/token_usage.js`**:
   - Added runtime-agnostic `base64EncodeUtf8(str)` and `buildContentsPutBody(o)` (`{ branch, message, content, sha? }`).
   - Added `--input <tempPath>` transport (`tempPutBodyPath`, `contentsPutInputCommand`, `tryPutViaInputFile`, `putTokenContents`) following the `checkRunStamp.js` pattern (`file_write` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input <tempFile>` + `file_delete` in `finally`), keeping the shell command string under 200 bytes regardless of payload size while preserving legacy `contentsPutCommand` fallback when `io.write` is not injected.
2. **`js/factory/token_usage_publish.js`**:
   - Wired `file_write` and `file_delete` into the `publishTokenUsage` IO adapter alongside `cli_execute_command` and `file_read`.
3. **`scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`**:
   - Replaced `-f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)"` with temp files (`jq -n --rawfile next ... '{branch, message, content: ($next | @base64)}'` + `gh api -X PUT ... --input "${BODY_FILE}"`).
4. **`js/unit-tests/test_factoryTokenUsage.js`**:
   - Added unit tests for `base64EncodeUtf8` (ASCII, padding, multi-byte UTF-8), `buildContentsPutBody`, `--input` temp-file lifecycle, and a >100 KB raw JSON (>131,072 bytes base64) regression test verifying the shell command stays <200 bytes.

Closes #1152"
  }
}
